solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who has faith in agent lives for conversion!

indicators.note: conversion here means changing form, so the letters of the two words are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a believer has handed their life to a secret agent for a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for conversion' rearranges AGENT and LIVES; the religious surface makes 'conversion' look like part of the picture rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is a zealous believer who preaches and spreads their faith.

clue.text: Retire from former sources of income and tips

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so take the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone stepping away from their old earnings and gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sources of' picks the first letters of 'income' and 'tips', I and T, after EX for 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave or withdraw, the same as to retire from a place.

clue.text: A cynic with no source of pride practising self-denial

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word for cynic

parts.note: a sceptic is a doubter, a near synonym of cynic

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here the P of pride

explanation.surface: A cynic who has lost all pride and lives austerely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes the P that 'source of' picks from 'pride'; the cynic's synonym is a doubter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic person lives a life of austere self-discipline, renouncing comforts and pleasures.

clue.text: Incredibly large after finishing off bag of fine food

indicators.note: after places the word for incredibly large behind the letter from bag
the finish of a word is its last letter, so take the end of bag

parts.note: astronomical figures are enormously large ones

explanation.surface: Something huge follows the polishing off of a bag of gourmet food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing off' gives G, the last letter of 'bag'; 'after' puts ASTRONOMICAL behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomical describes gastronomy, the art of good eating, so it relates to fine food.

clue.text: Oddly effete, accepted by mistress, and unconsumed

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the odd letters go inside the word for mistress

parts.note: a lover can be a mistress, a partner in an affair

indicators.note: oddly signals taking the first, third and fifth letters of effete

explanation.surface: An effete man taken up by a mistress, and somehow left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'effete'; 'accepted by' sets them inside the mistress word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover food is what remains uneaten, so it is unconsumed.

clue.text: Creatures from the deep lagoons outside

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea

indicators.note: outside here means the outermost letters of lagoons, its first and last

explanation.surface: Animals of the ocean depths found around lagoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creatures from the deep' reads as one definition, but only 'Creatures' defines; 'the deep' gives SEA and 'outside' takes L and S from 'lagoons'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals are marine animals, so they are creatures.

clue.text: Roll up in coat, and leave at the outset

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur

indicators.note: at the outset means at the start, so take the first letter of leave

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrap yourself in a coat and depart promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' takes L from 'leave' after FUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To furl a sail, umbrella or flag is to roll it up neatly.

clue.text: A French family eating some finally — but it's dirty

parts.note: un is the French for a or an

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the clan word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of some

explanation.surface: A French family scoffing a little food, though the place is filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives the end of 'some'; 'eating' puts it inside the family word, after the French for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean is a straightforward synonym of dirty, meaning not clean.

clue.text: Item underpriced in a seller's do, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words are only a possible version of the answer, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bargain item on offer at a retailer's sales party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'do' looks like a shop's event, but 'perhaps' rearranges A, SELLER'S and DO; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss leader is a product sold below cost to lure customers into a shop.

clue.text: People annexed by Spain (Castille)

indicators.note: annexed by means held within, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A nation taken over by Spain, specifically Castile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annexed by' means the letters sit in spaIN CAStille. The Spanish conquest of Peru makes the surface historically apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were a South American people whose empire Spain conquered.

clue.text: Panics, pinching sailor's biscuits

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so the word for panics goes round the sailor

parts.note: to flap is to panic, so flaps means panics
Jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone in a flap steals a seaman's biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' puts the sailor inside the panics word. In Britain a flapjack is an oaty baked bar, not a pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: British flapjacks are chewy oat bars, loosely counted among biscuits and bakes.

clue.text: The right thing to be done with mere parking fine?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for exactly what is needed or wanted
read literally, just means mere and a ticket is a parking fine, so it is only a ticket

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom word by word: 'just' as 'merely' and 'the ticket' as a parking penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for exactly what is wanted, the ideal thing.

clue.text: Cat that's a slow mover's worst nightmare?

parts.note: a tortoise is the proverbial slow mover; the possessive gives the final S
hell is the worst imaginable experience

explanation.surface: A joke asking which cat a tortoise would dread most.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half of the clue as a slow mover's worst nightmare, with an apostrophe after the reptile; the whole names a mottled cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with a mottled black, orange and cream coat.

clue.text: African city total is a pair of graduates

parts.note: to total figures is to add them up
taken as written

indicators.note: a pair of means two copies of the degree abbreviation

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A city whose total population is just two university graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' doubles BA, the Bachelor of Arts degree, giving BABA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia in East Africa.

clue.text: List in reportedly expensive vessel

indicators.note: in places the tilt word inside the sound-alike word
reportedly means as said aloud, so take the word sounding like the one for expensive

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive
a ship lists or cants when it tilts to one side

explanation.surface: A list kept inside a costly container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' swaps the word for expensive for its sound-alike animal; 'in' sets a ship's tilt inside it. 'List' looks like a roll of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel for serving wine or spirits.

clue.text: Almost tolerate the last letter — with a bit of poetry

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for tolerate loses its final letter

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Putting up with the letter Z in a short poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the D from STAND; 'the last letter' of the alphabet is Z; A is given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a verse of a poem, a section of poetry.

clue.text: Bench may be not as stern initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the stern word comes before the other

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
less means not as much, so not as gives less

explanation.surface: A judge's bench perhaps being less severe at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bench' suggests judges and 'stern' severity, but stern is the rear of a boat; 'initially' puts BACK first.
explanation.definitionFit: Many benches have no backrest, so a bench may be backless.

clue.text: Revenue for the writer on popular company

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the writer's word follows the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the writer refers to the setter, who is me

explanation.surface: Earnings for an author working with a well-known firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the setter's own pronoun after the other two pieces, as in a down entry or an across sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received, which is revenue for a person or business.

clue.text: Devices that stop Conservative and Unionist members of the upper classes

parts.note: toffs is British slang for posh, upper-class people

explanation.surface: Political figures from the posh classes who block things.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFFS is British slang for rich, upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off is a device that interrupts or stops a flow, such as a valve or switch.

clue.text: Totally unworried about a heartless official in game

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter, here the middle E

parts.note: a referee is the official in charge of a game

explanation.surface: A relaxed attitude towards a cruel referee during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central letter out of the game official; 'about' is c, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from anxiety, wholly without worries.

clue.text: Queen wears rocks and jackets

indicators.note: wears means has on, so the rocks word takes the queen's letters within it

parts.note: reefs are ridges of rock in the sea
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen sports jewels and coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' places the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina inside the rocks; 'rocks' tempts as slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket, originally worn by sailors.

clue.text: Direction in which new cocktail is stirred?

indicators.note: a stirred drink has its contents mixed about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Which way to swirl a newly made cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' mixes the letters of NEW, COCKTAIL and IS; the cocktail surface makes 'stirred' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticlockwise is a rotational direction, opposite to the hands of a clock.

clue.text: Speak for traitor held in empty office

indicators.note: held in means enclosed, so the traitor goes inside the emptied office
empty means remove the contents, leaving the outer letters of office

parts.note: a rat is someone who betrays others

explanation.surface: Speaking up for a traitor jailed in a deserted office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves O and E from 'office'; 'held in' puts RAT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally and at length, as in a speech.

clue.text: Vehicle entered in sales ledger

indicators.note: entered in means written within, so the answer is found inside the next words

explanation.surface: A car recorded in a company's sales book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered in' means the letters sit across saleS LEDger.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled is a vehicle on runners for travelling over snow.

clue.text: A new leaf — if it becomes a branch

indicators.note: new suggests the words taking a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Turning over a new leaf, as a leaf becomes part of a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges A, LEAF and IF IT; the tree picture hides the corporate verb sense, joining a larger body as one of its offshoots.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to affiliate is to attach oneself to a larger organisation, joining it as a subsidiary.

clue.text: King Charles II's lover's ring

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was the famous mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: The ring given by King Charles II to his mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn, the Restoration actress, was mistress of Charles II; 'ring' here is a bell's sound, not jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the solemn ringing of a bell, especially for a death.

clue.text: Part of church article rejecting second sight

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the second-sight letters are read backwards

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is second sight

explanation.surface: A church passage dismissing clairvoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns extrasensory perception round; 'second' is part of a phrase, not an S.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Made to feel dense — is it so bad without love?

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asking if being so thick is a terrible thing when unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges DENSE IS IT SO 'without' O (love, zero in tennis): drop the O and shuffle the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitised means made sensitive or aware, so made to feel.
